name: How do luxury home builders estimate square-foot pricing accurately?

mainEntity.name: Why is square-foot pricing so misleading for custom luxury homes?
mainEntity.text: Why is square-foot pricing so misleading for custom luxury homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Square-foot pricing is useful as a rough starting point, but it can hide major differences in real project cost. Luxury homes vary widely based on foundation complexity, glazing, cabinetry, mechanical systems, ceiling heights, structural spans, and the amount of custom finish work. A 4,000-square-foot house on a flat lot with modest detailing may cost far less than a similar-size home on a hillside with imported stone and custom steel. That is why the best builders estimate from scope, not just area. Homeowners should ask what assumptions are built into the price per square foot, including level of finish, site conditions, and allowances. A good estimate should make the cost drivers visible instead of reducing the project to one number.
acceptedAnswer.description: Square-foot pricing is often misleading because two homes with the same size can have very different costs based on site conditions, structure, finish level, and systems. A luxury home with custom millwork, large spans, premium glazing, and complex foundations will cost far more than a simpler build of the same size. Total scope matters more than size alone.
